issues.issue: The parenthetical "(the \"Maturity Date\")" is attached to the extension period rather than to the expiry date, so it is unclear whether the Maturity Date is December 31, 2014 or the extended date.
"Maturity Date" is defined here and then defined again in the prepayment bullet as "the last day of the Note's term", giving the same term two definitions within one provision-set.

"[N]ot be less than 8% on an annualized basis for a calendar year" does not say whether the 8% floor applies to each quarterly rate or only to the blended rate over a calendar year, and it is set against a rate fixed "in the sole discretion of the Manager".

The floor stated here conflicts with the Executive Summary, which describes the same rate as "subject to a minimum average rate of eight percent (8%) annualized"; a floor and an average minimum are different obligations.

The unqualified promise of quarterly Interest payments sits against the "insufficient funds" bullet, which contemplates pro rata payment when funds are short, and against the Roll-over Interest election.
"[Q]ualified investor" is used as the eligibility test but is nowhere defined; the Memorandum elsewhere uses "accredited investor" and the Section VIII suitability criteria.

This bullet defines "Maturity Date" as the last day of the Note's term, whereas the term bullet has already used "(the \"Maturity Date\")" in connection with the December 31, 2014 expiry and six-month extension.

Pro rata sharing on a shortfall is difficult to reconcile with the senior-priority rights conferred on a Company Borrowing lender and on the Collateral Agent's costs, both of which take ahead of Noteholders.

The promise that repayment "shall be secured by an interest in the assets of the Company" is qualified by "Company Borrowings", under which Noteholders agree a lender may take a senior security interest in all or some of the same Collateral.
"[Q]ualified investor" is the stated condition for additional purchases but is defined nowhere in the Memorandum.
The Company's records, rather than a reissued Note, evidence the increased Principal, which sits awkwardly with the "Payment for Notes" term under which the Note itself states the Principal amount.

The account is described as "a pooled account that is held in the Company's name" yet dedicated to "the exclusive purpose" of holding subscription deposits and "separate from the Company's general accounts"; whether this creates a trust or merely a Company account is left open.

This account is required to be "segregated" while the parallel Closing Account for initial subscriptions is described as "pooled", though both are said to be separate from the Company's general accounts.

"Minimum Holding Period" is defined by reference to the date of the requested prepayment rather than the date of the request, so it is unclear when a Noteholder may make the request as opposed to receive payment.

The Executive Summary states the same restriction differently — a Noteholder "may not request prepayment of a Note until it has held the Note for a minimum of one year" — and omits the sixty-day notice and quarter-end conditions imposed here.

The Collateral Agent must act "on terms required by the Manager ... but only to the extent that such terms or actions are not prohibited under the Noteholder Agreements", a proviso that refers back to agreements not before the reader and leaves the agent's actual authority indeterminate.

The authority to consent on Noteholders' behalf to subordination of the Collateral is difficult to reconcile with "Restricted Actions", which bars the Company from creating or suffering any Lien on the Collateral without approval of a Majority in Interest.

The >50% consent threshold here excludes Notes held by affiliates from the calculation, whereas "Majority in Interest" as defined in "Restricted Actions" contains no such exclusion; two different majority tests operate in the same instrument.

The exception for obligations "assumed by an affiliate of or successor in interest to the Company" has no stated conditions — no consent, no creditworthiness test — so the acceleration right can be defeated by an assumption the Noteholders never approved.

This acceleration term is the only stated event of default in the Memorandum, yet other provisions (e.g. the Collateral Agent substitution term) refer to periods when "the Company is in default under the Notes" without defining default.
New members may be admitted "with the requisite approval of members", a requirement stated without any specified threshold or source.

The Initial Closing is fixed at December 1, 2007 with a final closing at the end of the sixth full quarter (estimated June 30, 2009), while the Executive Summary states the initial closing will be "on or before December 3, 2007" with closings "through May 1, 2009".

The fee is payable in advance on Portfolio Loans "held on the last day of the preceding month", which the Section III compensation table restates identically but labels a "Portfolio Management Fee" — the term used in "Restricted Actions" and nowhere defined here.

"[O]perating, legal and administrative expenses of the Company, other than those borne by the Company or Servicer" is circular: the exception is defined by reference to the very allocation the sentence is making.

The cap "not to exceed a maximum of $500,000 or 1% of aggregate Principal of outstanding Notes, whichever amount is greater" is placed so that it may qualify only "organizational fees and costs" or the whole list of Company Expenses that follows.
The Section III compensation table describes Company Expenses in the same words but contains no dollar cap at all, so the two statements of the same defined term differ.
The estimate of "approximately $1,000 -$2,000 per Portfolio Loan" differs from the Section III compensation table, which anticipates these fees will "average approximately $1,000 per loan".

The direction that "[a]ny of such fees or commissions paid to the Company ... shall be paid to Servicer" sits against "Loan Brokerage Commissions, Renewal and Forbearance Fees" in Section III, which treats such fees as reducing the Company's return rather than as Company property to be handed over.

The defined term appears here as "Loan Service Expenses" but the Section III compensation table defines the same allocation as "Loan Service Expenses" against a heading of "Portfolio Service Expenses", leaving the scope of what the Servicer bears imprecise.

"[O]r other fees" is an open catch-all after a list of specific fee types (construction management, development, placement, origination, brokerage), leaving the permitted affiliate compensation effectively unlimited.
The permission is made "subject to restrictions with respect to Affiliated Transactions", a capitalised term that is defined nowhere in the Memorandum.

The sentence says the Company is restricted "in the amount of compensation it may receive", but the restrictions described elsewhere govern compensation paid by the Company to the Manager and Servicer, so the subject appears to be wrong.

"[W]ill terminate at the Manager's election upon the first to occur of" is internally inconsistent: it is unclear whether termination is automatic on the earlier event or requires an election the Manager may withhold.
A term ending two years after the Notes' Maturity Date is hard to reconcile with "Terms of Loans", which permits Portfolio Loans of up to six years made at any point during the offering period.

"[E]xcept for certain transfers to family trusts, to wholly-owned affiliates or by operation of law" leaves "certain" undefined, so which transfers escape the consent requirement cannot be determined from the text.

The cover-page legend states that Notes may not be transferred "EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN THE NOTE PURCHASE AGREEMENT", and the Executive Summary says transfers are permitted only "in the discretion of the Manager", with no exceptions.

The Noteholders' agreement that a Company Borrowing may take a senior security interest in the Collateral conflicts with "Restricted Actions", which forbids the Company to create or suffer any Lien on the Collateral without approval of a Majority in Interest.

"[A]mong other restrictions" leaves the enumerated list of restricted actions open-ended, so it cannot be determined whether the specific list is exhaustive of the matters requiring Majority in Interest approval.

The bar on the Manager "[w]ithdraw[ing] as the sole manager of the Company" without Noteholder approval conflicts with the Section III statement that the Manager and Servicer "retain the right to terminate all or any portion of their business relationship with the Company at any time".
"[S]uch of its business time ... as may be necessary" fixes no measurable commitment, and "similar enterprises to the Company" is garbled (apparently "similar to those of the Company").

"[T]imely information reasonably necessary for the preparation of income tax returns" is the only firm reporting obligation; all other reports and financial statements are left to the Manager's discretion, so the provision promises nothing determinate.

Words are missing after "Majority in Interest of Noteholders" — the sentence never says what "(i) violates" or "(ii) modifies", so as written the amendment restriction has no subject and cannot be applied.

The provision conditions amendment on the Company's obligations under the "Investor Documents", a term used nowhere else; the Memorandum defines "Offering Documents" and "Noteholder Agreements" instead.

The requirement of Majority in Interest approval for any modification of the Noteholder Agreements is in tension with the cover-page reservation of the Manager's "RIGHT TO MODIFY ANY OF THE TERMS OF THE OFFERING AND THE OFFERING DOCUMENTS".

The indemnity carve-out here is "willful misconduct or gross negligence", whereas Section III describes the Operating Agreement's indemnity as conditioned on the absence of "fraud, bad faith or willful misconduct" — two different standards for the same protection.

The power of attorney is granted by Noteholders under the Note Purchase Agreement but is expressed to cover "documents that the Members have expressly agreed to execute", although "Company Members" states that Noteholders are not admitted as members.

The intention to treat the Notes as indebtedness rather than equity is consistent with the creditor-status provisions, but the same document acknowledges throughout that recharacterisation as equity is possible.

Treating the Notes as "contingent debt instruments" for tax purposes is difficult to square with the Note Terms, under which Interest is a Floating Rate with an 8% floor rather than a contingent payment.
The provision uses "Comparable Yield" throughout but then refers to a "higher or lower Comparative Yield", an inconsistent term for the same concept.

The statement that the 8% Comparable Yield "does not constitute a projection or representation as to the amounts that Noteholders will actually receive" sits against the Note Terms' 8% rate floor and the Executive Summary's 8% target return.
The abbreviation is introduced as "(UBT)" but the concept is referred to as "UBTI" in every later paragraph.
The paragraph refers to an equity investment "in the Fund", a term the Memorandum never defines; the defined issuer is "the Company".

The passage is internally contradictory: it says that on recharacterisation amounts received "would not be treated as UBTI", then immediately explains circumstances in which the same income would generate UBTI.
It describes "the fixed payments provided for in the Notes", although the Note Terms provide for a variable Floating Rate set quarterly in the Manager's sole discretion.
